what: The Rent vs Buy Calculator compares two paths over the same number of years: buying a home with a mortgage, or renting and investing the money you would otherwise put into the home.
It counts the mortgage, property tax, upkeep, insurance, fees, buying and selling costs, home value growth, rent increases and the return on invested savings, then shows who ends up with more.
uses: See if buying beats renting for how long you will stay.
Learn how many years it takes for buying to pay off.
See what happens if prices rise slowly or fall.
See the first-month cost to own next to your rent.
See the cash needed up front.
tutorial: Enter "How many years you will stay".
Enter the "Home price", "Down payment (%)", "Mortgage interest" and "Mortgage term".
Enter buying and selling costs as % of price, property tax and upkeep as % per year, home insurance per year and any service fees per month.
Enter "Home value growth (% per year)". Negative values are allowed.
Enter "Monthly rent", "Rent increase", renter's insurance and the "Investment return on savings".
The line above the results says which path leaves you better off and by how much.
See the break-even year, the chart and the year-by-year table, and download it as CSV.
features: Both people start with the same cash and invest any monthly difference.
Mortgage, tax, upkeep, insurance, fees, buying and selling costs.
Home value, rent and investments grow at the rates you choose.
Shows when buying starts to win, if it does.
Two lines show buyer and renter wealth each year.
About 40 currencies or your own symbol.

example.title: Simple check
example.text: Buy a 120,000 home with cash and no costs or growth, or rent for 1,000 a month, over 1 year with 0% investment return. The buyer spends nothing each month, so saves the 12,000 rent: wealth 120,000 + 12,000 = 132,000. The renter keeps the 120,000 cash: wealth 120,000. Buying leaves you 12,000 better off.

tips: Be realistic about how long you will stay; buying usually needs several years to beat renting.
Upkeep of 1% of the home value a year is a common rule of thumb.
Try lower home growth and higher rates to stress-test the decision.
Include all buying costs such as taxes on purchase, legal and survey fees.
problems: I see a dash and a red message
A box is missing or out of range, such as a down payment above 100%. Fix the box named in the message.
The break-even says "Not within" the years
Buying does not catch up within your time frame. Try staying longer or adjusting the numbers.
My bank's mortgage payment is different
Banks may add insurance, fees or a different compounding. The payment here is principal and interest only.
